q: Carl Rogers' idea that a child needs acceptance regardless of behaviour is called
exp: Rogers held that unconditional positive regard promotes a healthy self-concept.

q: Which is a major cause of juvenile delinquency?
options: Neglect, broken homes and bad company
exp: Family disorganisation and bad peers contribute strongly.

q: Which attitude of a teacher towards gender or caste differences is professionally correct?
options: Treat all learners equally and avoid stereotypes
exp: Equity and non-discrimination are central to teaching ethics.

q: The Braille system for the visually impaired was invented by
exp: Louis Braille developed the six-dot tactile system.

q: An eclectic approach to counselling was advocated by
exp: Thorne combined directive and non-directive techniques.

q: Smooth transitions between activities in a lesson help to
exp: Kounin found that smoothness prevents disruptions.

q: Match the person with the institution: (1) Gandhi (2) Tagore; (a) Sevagram / Wardha basic school (b) Santiniketan.
exp: Gandhi's Nai Talim was based at Wardha and Sevagram; Tagore established Santiniketan.

q: Aurobindo advocated which medium for early education?
exp: He insisted that the mother tongue should be the medium.

q: The four pillars of education in the Delors Commission report are learning to know, learning to do, learning to live together and
exp: The report 'Learning: The Treasure Within' lists these four pillars.

q: According to Section 14, admission to school shall not be denied because of
options: lack of proof of age or birth certificate
lack of seats in the class
late payment of fees by parents
exp: Age proof cannot be a ground for denying admission.

q: Gesell's theory of development stresses mainly the role of
exp: Gesell held that development follows an inner maturational timetable; training cannot hasten it much.

q: A four-year-old says, 'The sun is sleeping because it is night.' This reflects
exp: Animism is attributing life and feelings to inanimate objects, common in the preoperational stage.

q: Which book is associated with Vygotsky?
options: The Language and Thought of the Child
exp: Vygotsky's 'Thought and Language' discusses the relation between speech and thinking.

q: Match the level with its description: (1) Preconventional (2) Conventional (3) Postconventional; (a) rules and social order (b) universal principles (c) punishment and reward.
exp: Preconventional is based on consequences, conventional on social rules, postconventional on principles.

q: Which teacher behaviour best supports Erikson's school-age stage?
options: Giving tasks that can be completed successfully and praising effort
exp: Experiences of competence lead to industry rather than inferiority.

q: Programmed instruction and teaching machines were developed on the basis of the ideas of
exp: Skinner advocated small steps, immediate feedback and reinforcement.

q: Match the theorist with the idea: (1) Tolman (2) Bruner (3) Ausubel; (a) discovery learning (b) latent learning (c) advance organisers.
exp: Tolman: latent learning and cognitive maps; Bruner: discovery; Ausubel: meaningful learning with advance organisers.

q: The Yerkes-Dodson law says that
options: moderate arousal gives the best performance on complex tasks
higher anxiety always gives better performance
arousal has no effect on performance
exp: Performance follows an inverted U-shape with arousal.

q: The term 'Intelligence Quotient' was first used by
exp: Stern, a German psychologist, introduced the ratio of mental age to chronological age.

q: Gordon's 'synectics' is a method that develops creativity through
options: analogies and metaphors in group problem-solving
exp: Synectics joins different elements using analogy.

q: Cattell's personality inventory is known as
exp: Cattell identified 16 source traits and developed the 16 Personality Factor Questionnaire.

q: Which is the BEST preventive step against substance abuse among adolescents?
exp: Awareness, life skills and guidance reduce risk.

q: Multi-level (tiered) tasks in a class help mainly to
exp: Tiered tasks let each learner work at a suitable level.

q: Which statement correctly differentiates integration from inclusion?
options: Inclusion modifies the school to fit the child, while integration expects the child to adapt
Inclusion keeps children in special schools
exp: Inclusion restructures school systems for all learners; integration places children in regular school with limited change.

q: Assertion (A): Group guidance is economical and useful. Reason (R): It can give common information to many students at the same time. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
exp: Career talks and orientation save time and resources.

q: In the 'ripple effect' as described by Kounin,
options: noise spreads from one room to another
a teacher's correction of one student influences nearby students' behaviour
exp: Handling misbehaviour of one student affects others.

q: Tagore's Sriniketan was meant for
exp: Sriniketan, founded in 1922, worked on rural development.

q: Match: (1) Vivekananda (2) Aurobindo (3) Gandhi; (a) Integral education (b) Nai Talim (c) Man-making education.
exp: Vivekananda: man-making; Aurobindo: integral; Gandhi: Nai Talim.

q: Constructivism in education holds that
options: learners construct knowledge from their experiences
exp: Learners actively create meaning by relating new ideas to prior knowledge.

q: Section 4 of the RTE Act provides for
options: special training for out-of-school children to bring them to age-appropriate class
exp: Out-of-school children are admitted to age-appropriate class with special training.
